title: 满江红
author: Yue Fei

translation: My hair bristles with rage beneath my helmet
Leaning on the railing, the drizzling rain has ceased
Thirty years of fame and deeds — dust and dirt
Eight thousand li of marching — clouds and moon
Grieving in vain over white hair
I'll crush the gap in the Helan Mountains
Hungry, we feast on the flesh of the invaders
Laughing, we quench our thirst with their blood
Wait until we rebuild the old rivers and mountains
And pay tribute at the heavenly palace

annotations.怒发冲冠: hair bristling with rage, lifting the helmet — pure fury
annotations.靖康耻: the Humiliation of Jingkang (1127) — Jurchens captured the Song capital and two emperors
annotations.雪: here a verb — to wipe away, to avenge
annotations.贺兰山: the Helan Mountains — here standing for enemy territory
annotations.朝天阙: to pay tribute at the imperial palace — to return victorious

appreciation: Attributed to the general Yue Fei, this is China's anthem of patriotic fury. The structure mirrors its emotion: the first half is the oath of a soldier ('don't idle away your youth, grieving in vain over white hair'), the second half is the vow of vengeance for the fall of the capital. Its imagery is deliberately shocking — the fury of a nation that lost its emperors and half its land. Whatever the debates about its authorship, it has been memorized by generations as the voice of loyalty itself.
